text: Suppose Aziz is at the MyID step, on the way to his first transfer.
prefix: Suppose Aziz is at the MyID step, on the way to his first transfer.

text: The mobile bank asks heeyID to open his MyID check.
prefix: The mobile bank asks heeyID to open his MyID check.

text: At that minute, MyID starts to answer slowly, and then not at all.
prefix: At that minute, MyID starts to answer slowly, and then not at all.

text: Aziz looks at a spinner.
prefix: Aziz looks at a spinner.

text: What happens to him, and what happens to the platform?
prefix: What happens to him, and what happens to the platform?

text: Lesson 3 named the services outside the bank, and Lesson 4 gave the configuration of the installation.
prefix: Lesson 3 named the services outside the bank, and Lesson 4 gave the configuration of the installation.

text: Here you see how the platform talks to those services, and what it does when one of them stops answering.
prefix: Here you see how the platform talks to those services, and what it does when one of them stops answering.

text: Start in the middle, with the core of heeyID.
prefix: Start in the middle, with the core of heeyID.

text: The core holds the rules: registration, proofing, devices and login.
prefix: The core holds the rules: registration, proofing, devices and login.

text: The core itself has no input and no output.
prefix: The core itself has no input and no output.

text: It never opens a connection, and it never calls MyID.
prefix: It never opens a connection, and it never calls MyID.

text: When it needs something from outside, it calls a port.
prefix: When it needs something from outside, it calls a port.

text: A port is a door in the words of the rules: open a proofing session, send a code, send a push.
prefix: A port is a door in the words of the rules: open a proofing session, send a code, send a push.

text: Behind each port is an adapter: the part that talks to one real service.
prefix: Behind each port is an adapter: the part that talks to one real service.

text: heeyID has four of them for the outside world: MyID, TAF, SMS and push.
prefix: heeyID has four of them for the outside world: MyID, TAF, SMS and push.

text: The TAF adapter calls the TAF agent inside the bank network.
prefix: The TAF adapter calls the TAF agent inside the bank network.

text: The other three go out through the egress proxy.
prefix: The other three go out through the egress proxy.

text: Each adapter runs as a unit of its own, and only the customer gateway and the workers call it.
prefix: Each adapter runs as a unit of its own, and only the customer gateway and the workers call it.

text: Now the tests.
prefix: Now the tests.

text: Each port has one real adapter, and no second version for the tests.
prefix: Each port has one real adapter, and no second version for the tests.

text: For the tests, a simulator takes the place of the outside service itself.
prefix: For the tests, a simulator takes the place of the outside service itself.

text: It speaks the same API as MyID, TAF, the SMS vendor or the push service.
prefix: It speaks the same API as MyID, TAF, the SMS vendor or the push service.

text: It gives every answer that the contract allows: success, each failure reason, a timeout and a service that is down.
prefix: It gives every answer that the contract allows: success, each failure reason, a timeout and a service that is down.

text: So the real adapter runs in every acceptance test, with no internet.
prefix: So the real adapter runs in every acceptance test, with no internet.

text: Each night, one more run goes against the MyID test environment.
prefix: Each night, one more run goes against the MyID test environment.

text: A team that tests only against the real service tests only the good days.
prefix: A team that tests only against the real service tests only the good days.

text: The simulator brings the bad days into every run.
prefix: The simulator brings the bad days into every run.

text: Now the walls around each call.
prefix: Now the walls around each call.

text: Each outgoing call has a timeout: how long the adapter waits for an answer.
prefix: Each outgoing call has a timeout: how long the adapter waits for an answer.

text: Each adapter also has a breaker.
prefix: Each adapter also has a breaker.

text: After a configured number of failures in a row, the breaker opens.
prefix: After a configured number of failures in a row, the breaker opens.

text: While it is open, calls fail at once, with no waiting.
prefix: While it is open, calls fail at once, with no waiting.

text: A test call goes to the service at a configured interval, and the breaker closes when the service answers again.
prefix: A test call goes to the service at a configured interval, and the breaker closes when the service answers again.

text: While the breaker is open, operations get an alert: a dependency is down.
prefix: While the breaker is open, operations get an alert: a dependency is down.

text: The timeouts and the breaker values are installation settings, like the MyID host in Lesson 4.
prefix: The timeouts and the breaker values are installation settings, like the MyID host in Lesson 4.

text: The panel cannot change them, and a change needs a new deployment.
prefix: The panel cannot change them, and a change needs a new deployment.

text: And now the most important rule: each outside service has one fixed behaviour when it is down.
prefix: And now the most important rule: each outside service has one fixed behaviour when it is down.

text: The adapter makes that behaviour impossible to bypass.
prefix: The adapter makes that behaviour impossible to bypass.

text: A timeout always gives one plain answer, never a raw error that each caller reads in its own way.
prefix: A timeout always gives one plain answer, never a raw error that each caller reads in its own way.

text: MyID is down: the customer sees that the service is temporarily not available.
prefix: MyID is down: the customer sees that the service is temporarily not available.

text: The customer stays at the current level, and the attempt does not count against the limits.
prefix: The customer stays at the current level, and the attempt does not count against the limits.

text: Nothing runs later in the background, so the customer starts the check again.
prefix: Nothing runs later in the background, so the customer starts the check again.

text: TAF is down: the code goes through the SMS service of the bank, and the attempt is not scored.
prefix: TAF is down: the code goes through the SMS service of the bank, and the attempt is not scored.

text: One refusal is not an outage: when the state services portal names another bank as the trusted bank, no code goes by SMS.
prefix: One refusal is not an outage: when the state services portal names another bank as the trusted bank, no code goes by SMS.

text: The SMS vendor is down: a code that needs an SMS cannot go now.
prefix: The SMS vendor is down: a code that needs an SMS cannot go now.

text: The notifications wait in Kafka, and go again later.
prefix: The notifications wait in Kafka, and go again later.

text: The push service is down: the notifications go by SMS only.
prefix: The push service is down: the notifications go by SMS only.

text: Back to Aziz and his spinner.
prefix: Back to Aziz and his spinner.

text: The MyID adapter waits for its timeout, then gives its plain answer: the provider is not available.
prefix: The MyID adapter waits for its timeout, then gives its plain answer: the provider is not available.

text: Aziz sees a short message, and his level does not move.
prefix: Aziz sees a short message, and his level does not move.

text: His attempt does not count.
prefix: His attempt does not count.

text: MyID fails for the next customers too, so the breaker opens.
prefix: MyID fails for the next customers too, so the breaker opens.

text: Now they get the same answer at once, with no spinner.
prefix: Now they get the same answer at once, with no spinner.

text: When MyID answers the test call again, the breaker closes, and Aziz starts his check again.
prefix: When MyID answers the test call again, the breaker closes, and Aziz starts his check again.

text: Two more rules keep the adapters safe.
prefix: Two more rules keep the adapters safe.

text: First, no adapter writes a request body or a response body to a log.
prefix: First, no adapter writes a request body or a response body to a log.

text: It writes the reference, the outcome and the time that the call took.
prefix: It writes the reference, the outcome and the time that the call took.

text: Second, hosts, ports and credentials come only from the installation configuration and Vault, never from the code.
prefix: Second, hosts, ports and credentials come only from the installation configuration and Vault, never from the code.

text: Each adapter holds only its own credential.
prefix: Each adapter holds only its own credential.

text: Now a check: TAF stops answering while a customer registers, so how does the code reach him?
prefix: Now a check: TAF stops answering while a customer registers, so how does the code reach him?

text: Through the SMS service of the bank, and that registration is not scored.
prefix: Through the SMS service of the bank, and that registration is not scored.

text: The core of heeyID has no input and no output.
prefix: The core of heeyID has no input and no output.

text: Four ports, four adapters, and a simulator for each outside service.
prefix: Four ports, four adapters, and a simulator for each outside service.

text: A timeout and a breaker on every call, and one fixed behaviour for each outage.
prefix: A timeout and a breaker on every call, and one fixed behaviour for each outage.

text: So Aziz waits a few seconds, not forever.
prefix: So Aziz waits a few seconds, not forever.

text: Each adapter holds one secret: the MyID credential, the TAF client secret, the SMS vendor login and the push credential.
prefix: Each adapter holds one secret: the MyID credential, the TAF client secret, the SMS vendor login and the push credential.

text: Lesson 6 shows where those keys live, and who holds them.
